articles.title: From iPhone Duo to Mac, Craft shows what a native productivity app can do
articles.description: It’s been a busy fall for Apple. iOS and macOS 27 arrived in September, iPhone Duo went on sale just a few days ago, and more Mac announcements are expected later this week. Between the new software and hardware, there’s plenty for Apple users to explore. Of all these announcements, the iPhone Duo has arguably attracted the most attention. As the first iPhone with a fundamentally different form factor, it introduces new possibilities for how we use our phones. But new hardware is only part of the story. Just as important is how apps take advantage of it. For an app like Craft, which brings notes, tasks, and documents together in one place, the larger display and new multitasking capabilities open up interesting new ways to work. Craft is ready for iPhone Duo from day one, with an interface designed to take advantage of its new form factor. And while the Duo is getting much of the attention right now, Craft has also seen a steady stream of improvements across iPhone, iPad, and Mac over the past few months. And there’s an additional bonus for anyone looking to give Craft a try: 40% off for life with code 9to5Mac40, available through this exclusive 9to5Mac offer. more…

articles.title: iPhone Duo is the most repairable foldable yet, but that's a very low bar
articles.description: A teardown of the new iPhone Duo shows multiple components that are easier to repair than on any previous foldable, but also many problem points. Taking apart the iPhone Duo - image credit: iFixit When iFixit tore down the iPhone 18 Pro, it gave it a "repairability" score of 7/10. By comparison, the iPhone Duo manages just 5/10, despite saying that there is much to admire in how Apple has designed it. The features that make the iPhone Duo better than all previous foldables include how the top layer of the screen can be relatively easily replaced. That compares to how with the original Samsung foldables, customers were destroying the screen by peeling off what appeared to be a packaging cover.
